product.lead: Clamp-on sensors go onto existing pipes. A model per measuring point learns the building's normal flow. A digital twin of the plumbing narrows a deviation to a riser or a building section. Alerts are reviewed with your maintenance team.

visual.alt: Diagram: a clamp-on sensor on a pipe sends readings into a live-flow chart with its learned baseline, a deviation is placed on the building's digital twin and raised as an alert.

install.h2: What does an install look like?
install.text: Ultrasonic flow sensors clamp onto the outside of existing pipes, pressure sensors onto existing taps. Under 15 minutes each, no pipe cutting, no shutdown of the water supply. From the sensor positions and the plumbing layout, AquaShield builds a digital twin of the building: which riser feeds which floors, which sensor sees which water. The model learns the building's normal flow from there. Your own team can clamp on the sensors.
install.visualAlt: Diagram: a clamp-on ultrasonic flow sensor on a riser and a pressure sensor on a tap.

labels.pressure: Pressure sensor on an existing tap

data.text: A dashboard with every measuring point, its live flow against its learned baseline, and the alert list ranked by severity. Each alert names the building, the riser or section, how far flow is from normal and for how long, and what to check first. Data coverage per site is shown so you know when a sensor is offline. Alerts go to the people you name. Nothing is sent before it has been reviewed.
data.visualAlt: Sample chart: one measuring point over seven days, the learned baseline band and a deviation on the last two days.

chart.title: Measuring point, riser B, seven days

precision.text: To the riser or the building section. The digital twin narrows a deviation to the place to check first, so the search starts at the right riser and the right floors instead of behind the first wet wall. Precision grows with every measuring point and every incident the model learns from.

ml.text: Each measuring point gets its own model. It learns that building's normal flow in 10-minute steps: night baseline, morning peak, weekday against weekend. A deviation is a flow pattern that normal does not explain. The digital twin maps which sensors see the same water, so a deviation can be placed in the network. Your team's feedback goes straight back into the model. Specialised machine learning for hydraulic systems, not a generic anomaly detector.
ml.visualAlt: Six measuring points, each with its learned baseline band and live flow. One riser departs from its baseline and is flagged.

faq.q: Does the install interrupt the water supply?
faq.a: No. Sensors clamp onto the outside of the pipe. The water stays on.

faq.q: How long does a rollout take?
faq.a: One building: one day of installs, the digital twin the same day, the model learns normal over the first weeks. A portfolio: building by building, at your pace.

faq.q: Does it work with old pipes?
faq.a: Yes. The sensors clamp onto any accessible pipe, old or new.
Alerts are ranked by severity and reviewed with your team before they escalate. Your feedback goes back into the model, so it gets sharper with every building.
You and the people you name. We do not sell data. See the privacy policy.
Priced per building and measuring point, a fraction of one claim. We quote from your plumbing plan.

realEstate.h1: Find the leak before your tenant does.
realEstate.lead: For portfolios with in-house maintenance, from hundreds to hundreds of thousands of units.

visual.alt: Six buildings of a portfolio, each watched by a riser sensor. One building shows a deviation on riser B and an alert names the floors to check first.

story.text: A tenant calls. A ceiling stains. Water shows up on a basement floor. By then the leak has been running for days or weeks. Finding it can take up to five site visits and a wall opened each time. Occupancy, energy and HVAC all have a live view. Water does not. AquaShield gives your maintenance team that view: every riser watched, deviations ranked by severity, and a location to check first.

faq.q: We have smart water meters. Is this the same?
faq.a: No. Meters count consumption per unit. AquaShield watches flow at the riser and learns what normal looks like, so it sees a leak that no single meter would.

faq.q: Do we need to open walls?
faq.a: No. Sensors clamp onto accessible pipe in risers, basements and shafts.

faq.q: What does our maintenance team have to do?
faq.a: Clamp on the sensors, or let us do it. Then act on the alerts: each one names the riser and the floors to check first.

faq.q: Does it work in old buildings?
faq.a: Yes. The sensors clamp onto any accessible pipe, old or new.
One. Roll out when you have seen it work.

faq.q: Can our insurer see the data?
faq.a: Only if you decide so. Some portfolios share it to negotiate terms. See the insurance page.

insurance.h1: Shorter loss duration. Lower claim severity.
insurance.lead: For property underwriters, claims and innovation leads who think in loss ratio, severity and risk data.

story.text: A hidden leak runs until someone notices. Every extra day adds secondary damage: subfloors, drywall, neighbouring units, business interruption. Earlier detection shortens the loss duration, and that is the lever on severity. Live flow data per riser adds a second value: a risk signal that underwriting does not have today, from buildings that are owner-operated and already instrumented.

dataCenters.h1: Catch the cooling‑loop leak before the outage.
dataCenters.lead: For facility and operations leads running liquid cooling, where water is not the pain. The outage is.

story.h2: Floor leak cables tell you after the fact.
story.text: A leak cable fires when water reaches the floor. By then a rack has lost cooling. Networked flow and pressure sensing per rack sees the deviation in the loop itself: a drop in pressure, a flow that does not match its neighbours. Clamp-on, non-invasive, no cutting into the cooling loop. The same model that learns a building's normal flow learns a cooling loop's.

status.h2: From residential risers to liquid cooling.
status.text: The sensors and the model that watch residential risers today go onto your cooling loop. First sites in Switzerland.
status.proof: Proof from real estate: live at a large residential portfolio in Germany since March 2026, 22 buildings and 32 measuring points.

together.h2: Let us try it together at your site.
together.text: One cooling loop, one rack row. Sensors clamp on, the twin maps the loop, the model learns its normal. You see the first alerts on your own racks.

visual.alt: Diagram: a row of liquid-cooled racks on one cooling loop, a clamp-on sensor on every rack branch, one branch showing a pressure drop.
visual.caption: Networked flow and pressure sensing per rack. Clamp-on, no cutting into the loop.
